original_recommendation.title: Resolve goal and product mismatch
original_recommendation.whats_happening: The account shows a primary goal of credit card signups while the offering listed is Personal Loans, creating risk that ads, landing pages, and tracking are misaligned.
what_you_should_do: Confirm the correct campaign objective (credit card signup vs personal loan) with stakeholders and document the single source of truth.
Update campaign naming, ad copy, and landing page messaging to match the confirmed offering and objective.
Pause or flag any ad groups/creatives that reference the wrong product until alignment is complete.
original_recommendation.why_this_matters: If creative and landing pages target the wrong product you will acquire the wrong leads, corrupt conversion data, and misstate ROAS for the intended product.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: Improved lead relevance, clearer measurement, and likely better conversion efficiency and ROAS once product and messaging are aligned.

original_recommendation.whats_happening: ROAS and CPA are reported but there is no margin, customer LTV, or target ROAS/CPA to judge profitability.
what_you_should_do: Request product margin, average customer lifetime value, and target ROAS/CPA from Finance or Product leadership.
Calculate a target CPA and target ROAS for the campaign and document tolerance ranges.
Apply these targets as guardrails in bidding strategies and budget allocations.
original_recommendation.why_this_matters: Without profitability targets you cannot determine whether the observed ROAS (1.8) or CPA ($16.74) is acceptable or needs improvement.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: Ability to optimize toward profitable acquisition rather than arbitrary efficiency metrics.

original_recommendation.title: Reconcile tracking and revenue fields
original_recommendation.whats_happening: Revenue fields are inconsistent (metrics.revenue is null while top-level revenue exists) and attribution method is not defined, reducing confidence in reported ROAS.
what_you_should_do: Run a tag and conversion audit across Google Ads and analytics to identify missing or broken revenue/event tags.
Ensure revenue value is passed into the ad platform for every conversion and reconcile the platform revenue to your backend records.
Decide and document the attribution model used for reporting (last-click, data-driven, etc.) and apply it consistently.
original_recommendation.why_this_matters: Accurate revenue and a consistent attribution model are needed to trust ROAS and to make correct bid and budget decisions.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: Restored confidence in ROAS and revenue metrics, enabling informed optimization and budgeting decisions.

original_recommendation.title: Reduce single-channel concentration risk
original_recommendation.whats_happening: Provided data only covers Google Search, so performance and cost swings on that single channel could materially affect results.
what_you_should_do: Design a 4–6 week test allocating a small percentage of budget (e.g., 10–15%) to one additional channel (display, social, or programmatic).
Use the same conversion definitions and reporting structure to compare CPA and ROAS across channels.
If new channel performance meets profitability targets, incrementally reallocate budget to diversify.
original_recommendation.why_this_matters: Diversifying reduces dependency on one channel and may uncover lower-cost sources of qualified leads.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: Lower overall business risk from channel concentration and potential discovery of more cost-efficient acquisition sources.

what_you_should_do: Enable and collect audience-level reporting in Google Ads and analytics (age, gender, device, location) for the campaign period.

original_recommendation.why_this_matters: Segment-level performance shows where to scale spend and where to cut back, improving efficiency without guessing.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: Improved targeting and budget efficiency through identification of higher-performing audience segments.

original_recommendation.title: Define conversion event and segment by lead quality
original_recommendation.whats_happening: The conversion definition is not provided, so it's unclear if reported conversions are qualified customers or preliminary leads.
what_you_should_do: Confirm the exact action counted as a conversion (e.g., form submit, approved application, click-to-call) and document it.
Create separate conversion actions for micro-conversions (lead captured) and macro-conversions (approved customer) with distinct values.
Map conversion statuses to downstream qualification data so you can report CPA/ROAS on qualified customers separately from raw leads.
original_recommendation.why_this_matters: Knowing which conversions are high-quality customers versus initial leads prevents over-optimizing for volume that doesn't convert to revenue.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: Cleaner optimization signals, better bid decisions, and improved alignment between ad spend and true customer acquisition.
